purpose: test the precondition of the single-origin motive claim: that 'god' names one concept across the traditions compared
method: curated analyst-authored regular-expression families matched against the eligible passages of the v2 corpus; frequencies, work attestation and regional attestation reported per family; no score, no composite, no threshold
measurement_unit: matched term occurrences per family, normalised per 10k eligible words

reproducibility.randomness: none: sorted iteration, no sampling, no fitted parameters

excluded_terms.\\bmana\\b: matches mana as a plural of man and appears in unrelated ethnographic prose
excluded_terms.\\bthe law\\b: matches Mosaic-law and secular-law prose indiscriminately
excluded_terms.\\bdivine\\b: matches polite formulae, honorifics and secular praise
excluded_terms.\\bgod\\b: the target word itself: frequency tracks book genre and translation style, not concept
excluded_terms.\\bemperor\\b: matches Roman and Japanese secular rulers

what_this_measures: the vocabulary available to nineteenth- and twentieth-century English translators and editors of these works, which is the only version of the concept this corpus can access
cannot_support: that a concept is absent from a tradition: absence of an English term in one translation is not absence of the idea, and this corpus is monolingual
that any tradition's adherents believe or do not believe anything; this is a text probe, not an interview or a ritual record
that one family is historically prior to another: attestation counts here are not dated
any conclusion about the existence or non-existence of supernatural beings, which no vocabulary census can address

that a matched negation is doctrine: 'if no god withstand' is a conditional, 'beside me there is no God' is exclusivist monotheism, and 'atheists' in the Mahābhārata names a school in a doxography rather than the author's belief. The families separate these only partially, and every record still needs source-critical review
that the families are exhaustive or non-overlapping; they are analyst-authored and would change under a second coders lexicon, which is the reliability test this probe lacks

one_concept_test.question: is there a divine concept shared by every part of this corpus?
one_concept_test.verdict: no family is attested in every indexed work, and the broadest reaches 13 of 14 regional labels. This is a vocabulary observation about English translations and nothing more. It is NOT evidence against a common origin: an inheritance-with-transformation hypothesis predicts divergence of surface forms, since abstraction, demotion, nominalisation and silencing are how concepts are transmitted; and every competing model (single origin, multiple origins, regional inheritance with mixing, independent convergence) predicts this same non-detection pattern, so the observation cannot rank them. Non-detection licenses only the report 'not detected in these sources'. See TRACK_B_METHOD_v2.md sections 3 and 8 for the frame that replaces these ten conflated grammars, and results/exclusivist_monotheism_audit.json for what the audit did to the oneness result below.

skepticism_evidence.note: Texts that deny or suspend belief in gods or a creator are the direct counterexample to universality, so they are recorded with locators. A negation is not enough: the monotheistic formula and comparative exaltation are excluded by the rules below, every excluded match is published rather than discarded, and every kept match is marked unreviewed, because a regular expression cannot decide whether a passage is doctrine, hypothetical, or polemic.

oneness_claim_distribution.question: the motive claim needs divinity to be one concept, and often borrows the doctrine that divinity is literally one as its evidence; this reports where that doctrine actually appears
oneness_claim_distribution.reading: oneness is unevenly distributed across this corpus, which is a descriptive result. It does NOT license the stronger sentence this field previously carried ('a doctrine of particular traditions rather than the shared kernel'): the four 'works attested' are not four independent witnesses. Eight of the nine sacred_books_east hits are Qur'an material reprinted inside Wilson's anthology, which already counts the translation they reprint, and the ninth is Thomas Carlyle's essay describing the formula rather than confessing it -- a dependence rule the census ignored. Two hits are substring collisions (1 Cor 6:17 'one spirit', 1 Ne 10:19 'one eternal round') that state nothing about divine oneness, and three are worship prohibitions whose wording presupposes the very gods they forbid. Matching after whitespace normalisation raises 46 hits to 51 and recovers Isaiah 44:6 and Mark 12:29, which the raw line-wraps had hidden. What survives is 34 confessional matches in two independent works, kjv_bible and quran_sale -- a file whose own title page prints Rodwell, not Sale, as its translator. See results/exclusivist_monotheism_audit.json for every match, locator, verdict and missed formula class.
